changes: Wired the canonical koala-residue gate (scripts/verify-koala-residue.mjs, from B-40eb) into the package.json test chain (the lattice validate fallback battery), and cleaned the last 7 residual koala-* mkdtemp prefixes on main (english-only-guards-smoke.ts x5, review-incremental-context-smoke.ts x2) -> lattice-*.
usage: The gate now runs on every `lattice validate` / `npm test` via the `test:koala-residue` step. Run `node scripts/verify-koala-residue.mjs` standalone to check active-scope koala-brand residue (PASS = 0 unclassified); `--self-test` runs 5 classify() unit tests.
expectedOutcome: node scripts/verify-koala-residue.mjs PASS 0 unclassified; npm test includes a passing test:koala-residue step; lattice validate all-green and exercises the gate.
actualTranscript: node scripts/verify-koala-residue.mjs -> PASS koala-residue: 0 unclassified; --self-test -> 5/5; npm test -> includes test:koala-residue PASS; npm run build -> exit 0; lattice validate -> ALL PASS.
outcomeDiff: none - expected matches actual; the gate is now continuous and green on main.
limitations: The gate scan scope is git-tracked/staged files only (a B-40eb design choice), so an untracked new file is not scanned until git add. The LEGACY_LOGIC_FILES allowlist may need refinement as new legacy-logic files appear.
pitfalls: When adding new smoke tests, do not use a koala-* mkdtemp prefix or the gate will flag it; use lattice-* prefixes. The gate runs inside npm test, so a broken gate script fails the whole test chain (intended, so the wiring cannot silently skip).
